OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Shri Shanti Tyagi, a former Member  of this House, on 3rd March, 2001, at 
the age of 80. 
Born in Village Kaithwari, District Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, in April, 1920, Shri 
Tyagi had his education at Meerut College, Meerut. 
An agriculturist by vocation, Shri Tyag i actively participated in the freedom 
struggle and was imprisoned several times between 1939 and 1946. He also took part 
in the historic Goa Liberation Movement. He authored several articles and booklets, 
in Hindi and English, on economic and political issues. 
Shri Tyagi represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House for two 
consecutive terms, from 3rd April, 1982 to 2nd April, 1988, and from 3rd April, 1988 
to 2nd April, 1994. During that period, he was a Member of various Parliamentary 
Committees. He took a keen interest in the proceedings of the House. 
In the passing away of Shri Tyagi, the country has lost a veteran freedom fighter 
and an eminent social worker. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Shanti Tyagi. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect 
to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 
MR.   CHAIRMAN:   Secretary-General   will   convey   to   the 
members of the bereaved family our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.

Installation of Ramps at World Heritage Sites for Disabled Persons 
*323. SHRIMATI JAYAPRADA NAHATA:  
         SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: 
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether her Ministry has taken up with the Archaeological Survey of India 
to install ramps at all world heritage sites and also at 34 national monuments for 
assisting disabled persons; and 
(b) if so, the response received, so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRIMATI MANEKA GANDHI): (a) and (b) The 
Ministry of Social Justice and 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [19 March, 2001] 
Empowerment has taken up with Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for providing 
barrier free facilities to the persons with disa bilities in the monumental structures and 
historical/heritage sites. 
The Archaeological Survey of India has decided that all important centrally 
protected monuments should be provided with a separate path-way at the entrance 
gate to facilitate persons with disabilities for their entry by a wheel-chair, wherever 
feasible. Wooden ramps will al so be provided with convenient slope. In addition to 
the above, all the "A" category monuments, i.e. monuments listed on the World

wheelchair. Directions to provide above facilities to the persons with disabilities in the 
important centrally protected  monuments in addition to all the 16 World Heritage

Study on Social and Financial Problems of Senior Citizens 
* 324. SHRI KHAGEN DAS:  Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND 
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of senior citizens in the country; 
(b) whether Government have carried out any study about the financial and 
social problems faced by them; and 
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government to give relief to them? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND 
EMPOWERMENT (SHRIMATI MANEKA GANDH I): (a) As per the 1991 Census 
the number of Senior Citizens aged 60+ in the country is 56,681,640. The population 
projections for 1996-2016 made by the Technical Group on Population Projections 
(1996) indicate that the 100 million mark is expected to be reached in 2013. 
(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. The Ministry  of Social Justice & Empowerment 
commissioned a project called OASIS (An acronym for Old Age Social & Income 
Security) and nominated an eight member Expert Committee headed by Dr. S.A. 
Dave, former Chairman of UTI, to examine policy questions connected with old 
6 

[19 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
age income security in India. The Committee has submitted its report to the 
Government on 11.1.2000. The Government is considering the recommendations of 
the Committee and no final decision has been taken on it. However, this Ministry has 
been implementing schemes to provide relief through voluntary organizations for 
setting old age homes, day care centers, mobile medical units etc.

(a) how far the special satellite channel for the North-East inaugurated on 
December 27, 2000, at Guwahati can cover the North-East region; 
(b) what arrangements have been made for the viewers to cover the different 
scheduled and major Indian languages spoken in this region;

(c) The Cable Television Network (Regulatio n) Act, 1995 is applicable to the

(d) While Guwahati and Agartala have High Power Transmitters for both DD-I 
and DD-2, all the other state capitals in

BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government would announce a new package for the North-East to counter 
the propaganda war by neighbouring countries like China, Myanmar and Bangladesh; 
(b) whether the new package would cover the television as well as radio network; 
(c) if so, by when; and 
(d) the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRIMATI 
SUSHMA SWARAJ): (a) to (d) The Government is already giving special attention the 
coverage of North-Eastern Region by AIR and DD. The AIR is implementing 18 projects in 
the North-Eastern Region under its Plan programme. DD is implementing projects for 9 
transmitters and 2 transposers for DD-I in the NER, under its Plan programme. These projects

local talent in programmes. A 24-hour NE channel is in operation. A sum of Rs. 4.2 crores 
has recently been released for software development. It is the constant endeavour of the 
Government to upgrade, enlarge and expand the package of programmes for the 
North-East for AIR and DD.

Impact of Rent Control Laws on Urban Development and Housing 
*328. SHRI SWARAJ KAUSHAL: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the impact of rent control laws on the urban development and housing in the 
country; 
(b) whether Government propose to make amendments in the law in Delhi and 
advise/suggest to the State Governments to make changes on the basis of the experience 
in this regard; and 
(c) if so, the details and broad outlines thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) to (c) Rent Control Legislation in many States 
has resulted in a freeze of rents, very low returns on investment and difficulty in resuming 
possession. It has also adversely affected investment in rental housing and caused 
deterioration of the rental housing stock. On the recommendation of a number of expert 
bodies, the Government decided to reform the rent legislation in the country in a way that

of both the Houses of Parliament in July, 1992. It was circulated to all the State

Control Legislation. Most of the State Governments have already initiated action in

Action plan for reducing poverty 
*330. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have recently formulated any comprehensive action plan for 
reducing poverty and developing a community-based service in the country through 
massive development programmes in the country; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHA N): (a) and (b) This Ministry has been 
implementing a specific programme for the alleviation of urban poverty called"Swama 
Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY)" with effect from 01.12.1997 on all India basis to 
provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed or underemployed poor (i) 
through encouraging' the setting up of self-employment ventures by those who have read 
upto 9th standard and (ii) through provisi on of wage employment for construction of 
socially and economically useful public assets. This programme relies on creation of 
suitable community structures and delivery of inputs through the medium of Urban 
Local Bodies (ULBs) and such Community Structures (CSs). This programme is funded 
in the ratio 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [19 March, 2001] 
of 75:25 between the Centre and the Stat es. Under SJSRY, Central funds amounting 
to Rs. 415.82 crores have been released to State/UT Governments upto February, 
2001. 
Proposal to End Shelterlessncss 
*331. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:  
          SHRI B. J. PANDA: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have a proposal to end shelterlessness by the end of 
Ninth Plan; 
(b) if so, the various housing schemes through which a house would be 
provided to every person in various States; 
(c) the progress thereof as on date. State-wise; and 
(d) the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) and (b) As per the projections made by 
the Working Group for the 9th Plan, a total of 16.76 million units would have to be 
constructed in the urban areas during the 9th Plan period for covering housing 
shortage. 
The National Housing & Habitat Policy, 1998 laid on the Table of the Lok 
Sabha & Rajya Sabha on 29.07.1998 envisages Government's role as an enabler 
rather than builder. Government aims to create an enabling environment by removing 
the legal, regulatory, technical, and financia l constraints facing the housing sectors. 
The State Governments are required to draw their own action plans to address the 
housing problems in their States. 
Housing is a State subject. There is no Central Sector Scheme for provision of 
houses in urban areas. However, in order to facilitate construction of adequate housing 
facilities, particularly for EWS and LIG, Government of India has launched the 2 
Million Housing Programme under which construction of 7 lakh houses in urban areas 
and 13 lakh in rural areas every year will be facilitated through State Government 
agencies on a demand-driven approach. At the present

needs of the poor in all States are largely met.

Coverage for remote areas of the country by Doordarshan 
*332. SHRI R.S. GAVAI: Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Prasar Bharati has formulated cost-effective strategies to extend 
Doordarshan coverage to the remote and sparsely populated regions of the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps mooted by the Prasar Bharati to exploit advantages of 
16 

[19 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
terrestrial broadcasting and use of local studio and programming personnel? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING SHRIMATI 
SUSHMA SWARAJ): (a) and (b) Doordarshan programmes are already available all 
over the country in satellite mode, and can be received using appropriate dish antenna 
systems or through cable networks. Terrestrial relay of Doordarshan currently covers 
about 88.9% of the country's population. In or der to spread the terrestrial coverage to 
more areas, including the remote and sparsely populated areas of the country, 
Doordarshan is currently setting up 185 transmitters. A number of factors, such as 
area/ population to be covered, costs involved, technological requirements, 
infrastructure facilities etc., are taken into consideration at the time of deciding upon 
the location and power of a transmitter. With the commissioning of projects presently 
under implementation, the population coverage is expected to go up to 91.3%. 
(c) Doordarshan is taking full advantage of the terrestrial network for 
broadcasting. Local studios are also utilised  to produce programmes. In the Regional 
Kendras, a large portion of allotted time is devoted to in-house programmes, which 
are produced with local participation.

In the literacy campaigns, the Scheduled Tribes are specially target ted. These 
campaigns reach out to areas of the country, which are most backward, i lliterate and

of 15—35   years   &   Continuing   Education   Schemes  of  the National Literacy 
Mission.
